summary.en: Bandits in Zamfara attacked a mosque during Subhi prayer, killing Governor Dauda Lawal's aide and abducting worshippers, while separate bandit raids killed a farmer after a N56 million ransom was paid. In Benue, gunmen shot a driver and abducted three passengers on a road convoy. The military rescued 119 abducted travellers and killed terrorists in a week of operations. President Tinubu publicly sought forgiveness for his absence after the Plateau attack and announced a five-year defence plan, while AI-generated disinformation is spreading ahead of the upcoming election. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter i Zamfara angrep en moské under Subhi-bønnen, drepte guvernør Dauda Lawals assistent og bortførte tilbedere, mens separate bandittraid drap en bonde etter at en løsepenger på N56 millioner ble betalt. I Benue skjøt væpnede menn en sjåfør og bortførte tre passasjerer på en veikonvoi. Militæret reddet 119 bortførte reisende og drepte terrorister i en uke med operasjoner. President Tinubu ba offentlig om tilgivelse for sin fravær etter Plateau-angrepet og kunngjorde en femårs forsvarsplan, mens AI-generert desinformasjon sprer seg før det kommende valget. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
